title: Fire Ships at Red Cliffs
text:
In the winter of 208, the warlord Cao Cao, master of northern China, came down the Yangtze with a huge army and fleet to finish off his southern rivals. Sun Quan and Liu Bei joined forces against him, with Sun Quan's general Zhou Yu in command. They were heavily outnumbered.

Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms says that Zhou Yu's officer Huang Gai noticed something about the enemy fleet: Cao Cao's ships were moored close together, bow to stern, and could be burned. Huang Gai sent Cao Cao a letter offering to defect with his ships. He then prepared a squadron of vessels packed with dry reeds and brushwood soaked in oil, covered with curtains and decked with flags, each towing a small fast boat behind it.

Huang Gai sailed toward Cao Cao's fleet with the wind behind him. Cao Cao's men came out to watch, thinking he was surrendering. Close to the line, his crews set the ships on fire and escaped in the small boats. The blazing ships drove into the packed fleet, and the fire spread to the camps on the shore. Many of Cao Cao's men burned or drowned. Weakened also by sickness in his army, Cao Cao retreated north. The battle ended his hope of uniting China and led to the division into three kingdoms.
lesson: A larger force often has a structural weakness that comes with its size. Find what makes the opponent strong and ask how that same feature could be turned against him.
people: Zhou Yu, Huang Gai, Cao Cao, Sun Quan, Liu Bei
location: Red Cliffs on the Yangtze (modern Hubei, China)
source: Chen Shou, Records of the Three Kingdoms (Sanguozhi), biography of Zhou Yu
caveat: The exact site of the battle is disputed, and the novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms added many famous details not in the history.
